text: Οὐρίας (Hebr.), Uriah, husband of Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon.
gloss: Uriah, husband of Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon

text: οὐσία, property.
ὀφειλέτης, (a) a debtor, one who owes, one who is indebted; (b) one who has sinned against another (an Aramaism, see ὀφείλημα), a sinner, Lk. xiii 4.
gloss: a debtor, one who owes, one who is indebted

text: ὀφειλή, a debt, what is owing (due): the mutual obligation of married life, 1 Cor. vii 3.
ὀφείλημα, (a) a debt; (b) in Aramaic the same word indicates a debt and a sin; hence a sin (probably as that for which we owe reparation to God or to another person).
ὄφελον (in origin an aorist of ὀφείλω, with augment dropped), I would that.
ὄφελος, advantage, gain.
ὀφθαλμοδουλεία, enslavement to the eye, the subjection that waits upon a glance of a master's eye.
note: headword printed ὀφθαλμοδουλεία

text: ὀφρύς, (properly the brow; hence) the brow, a ridge (of a mountain).
ὀχλέω, I trouble, torment, worry.
note: headword printed in active form ὀχλέω

text: ὀχλοποιέω, I gather a crowd.
ὀχύρωμα, a bulwark, a bastion: hence, met.
ὀψάριον, (conversational diminutive of ὄψον, seasoning [especially fish] taken as a relish with bread: hence) a relish; then especially, a fish.
ὀψέ, late: sometimes c. gen. either late on or after.
ὄψιμος, late in the year (opposite to πρόϊμος).
ὄψις, (a) the face; (b) the features, the outward appearance, John vii 24.
ὀψώνιον, especially plur. ὀψώνια, (rations: then) soldier's pay, Lk. iii 14, cf. 1 Cor. ix 7: pay, wages, salary, reward in general, Rom. vi 23, 2 Cor. xi 8; charges, 1 Cor. ix 7.
παγιδεύω, I ensnare, I entrap.
παγίς, a snare (especially for catching birds: perhaps a net thrown over one): hence, met., of moral snares.
πάγος: see Ἄρειος.
note: headword printed lower-case πάγος

text: παθητός (passibilis), capable of suffering.
πάθος, (properly experience, feeling; hence) passion, lustfulness, lust (as a state or condition).
παιδαγωγός (pedagogus), a boy-leader, a slave or freedman who attends and guards a boy to and from (sometimes also in) school, and looks after his moral character especially, a tutor.
παιδάριον (formerly a diminutive), either a boy or a slave.
gloss: either a boy or a slave

text: παιδευτής, one who disciplines, a trainer; almost a chastiser, Heb. xii 9.
παιδιόθεν, from childhood, from early boyhood.
παίζω, I play, I sport (includes singing and dancing).
παίω, I strike.
πάλαι, long ago, almost weakened to already in Mk. xv 44.
παλαιότης, oldness.
παλαιόω, I make old, I antiquate; I wear out; I treat as past, Heb. viii 13; pass. I fall to the past, Heb. viii 13.
πάλη, wrestling, a wrestling bout; hence a struggle, a conflict.

παλινγενεσία, (a) an eschatological term (used by Pythagoreans and Stoics, found in Josephus of the rebirth of the fatherland after the exile, and in Philo of the re-birth of the earth after the flood), in Mt. xix 28 for the current conception of the Messianic renewal of the world or of the people Israel, rebirth; (b) rebirth of the individual life following on or typified in baptism, Tit. iii 5.
note: headword printed παλινγενεσία; gloss is the English meaning at the end of sense (a)

text: Παμφυλία, Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
gloss: Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor

text: πανδοχεῖον, an inn, khan, hotel.
πανδοχεύς, an innkeeper, landlord, hotel-manager.
πανήγυρις; a festival assembly.
note: punctuation after headword printed as a semicolon

text: πανοικεί, with all (his) household.
πανοπλία, armour.
πανοῦργος, crafty (playfully used).
πανπληθεί, adv. lit. with the whole crowd, almost equivalent to a subject of the sentence.
note: headword printed πανπληθεί

text: πανταχῆ, everywhere.
note: headword printed πανταχῆ without iota subscript

text: παντελής; εἰς τὸ παντελές (omnino), utterly, at all, Lk. xiii 11; in Heb. vii 25 either entirely, or, more probably, for ever, finally.
πάντῃ, in every way.
πάντοθεν (undique), from all sides, from all quarters; on all sides.
gloss: from all sides, from all quarters

text: παραβαίνω, (a) I fall away, take a false step, Ac. i 25; (b) I overstep, transgress.
gloss: I fall away, take a false step

text: παραβάλλω, I cross over, I strike across.
gloss: I cross over, I strike across

text: παραβιάζομαι, I urge, press.
παραβολεύομαι, I expose myself (to danger).
παραδειγματίζω, I put to open shame.
παράδεισος, a quarter of heaven conceived by the later Jews to be in or just above the ‘third heaven’, paradise (lit. an enclosed orchard or garden with fruit trees).
note: gloss taken from the defining word, since the opening description runs well over 60 characters with no earlier comma

text: παράδοξος, unexpected; hence wonderful.
παραζηλόω, I make jealous, I provoke to jealousy.
gloss: I make jealous, I provoke to jealousy

text: παραθαλάσσιος, by the sea (lake), on the coast.
gloss: by the sea (lake), on the coast

text: παραθεωρέω, I look past, overlook, neglect.
παραθήκη (depositum), a deposit (properly of money or valuables deposited with a friend for safe-keeping, while the owner is abroad).
παραινέω, I admonish, advise.
παρακαθέζομαι, I sit beside.
παρακαλύπτω, I conceal, veil.
note: headword printed in active form παρακαλύπτω

text: παράκειμαι, I rest with.
παρακοή, disobedience.
παρακολουθέω, I accompany, follow closely, both lit. and met., I investigate; I result [Mk.] xvi 17 (v. l).
note: printed "(v. l)" without a stop after l

text: παρακούω, (a) I hear carelessly or incidentally, or I pretend not to hear, Mk. v 36; (b) I refuse to hear; I disobey.

παρακύπτω, I stretch forward the head to catch a glimpse (especially through a window or door, sometimes inwards, oftener outwards: fig. it implies a rapid, hasty, and cursory glance), I look, peep, peer in (at); I look down.
gloss: I stretch forward the head to catch a glimpse

text: παραλέγομαι (lego), I coast along, sail along.
παράλιος, on the sea-coast, on the sea-board: ἡ παράλιος (sc. χώρα), the coast country.
gloss: on the sea-coast, on the sea-board

text: παραλλαγή, a variation; hence, a periodic change of a heavenly body.
παραλογίζομαι, I deceive, beguile.
παραμένω, I remain beside, I stand by; hence equivalent to, I serve (as a free man), cf. perhaps Phil. i 25, James i 25; I remain in office, Heb. vii 23; I persevere in the law, James i 25.
gloss: I remain beside, I stand by

text: παραμυθέομαι, I encourage, comfort, console.
παραμυθία, encouragement, comfort, consolation.
παραμύθιον, consolation.
παρανομέω, I contravene a statute (law).
παρανομία, a breach of a statute (law).
παραπικραίνω, absol. I embitter, provoke, irritate.
παραπικρασμός, embitterment, provocation, irritation.
παραπίπτω, I fall back (into the unbelieving and godless ways of the old time).
παραπλέω, I sail past (without stopping there).
παραπλήσιον, in a manner like.
παραπλησίως, correspondingly, in like manner.
παραρέω, (lit. I flow past, I glide past, hence) I am lost, I perish, or merely, I drift away (I fall away) from duty (or the way of salvation).
note: headword printed παραρέω

text: παράσημος, a figure-head.
παρασκευάζω, I prepare; mid. I prepare, make preparations, 1 Cor. xiv 8.
παρασκευή, the day of preparation, the day before the sabbath, Friday.
gloss: the day of preparation, the day before the sabbath, Friday

text: παρατείνω, I prolong.
παρατηρέω, act. and mid. (a) I watch carefully, keep my eye on (as a cat does a mouse); absol. I watch my opportunity, Lk. xx 20; (b) I observe, keep, Gal. iv 10.
gloss: I watch carefully, keep my eye on
note: entry runs onto page 199

text: παρατήρησις, a watching for.
παρατυγχάνω, I come by chance, I am by chance in a certain place.
gloss: I come by chance, I am by chance in a certain place

text: παραυτίκα, adv. with force of adj., present, immediate.
παραφέρω, I turn aside, I cause (suffer) to pass by, Mk. xiv 36, Lk. xxii 42; I carry away, remove, lit. or met.
gloss: I turn aside, I cause (suffer) to pass by

text: παραφρονέω, I am out of my senses.
gloss: I am out of my senses

text: παραφρονία, madness.
παραχειμάζω (hiberno), I spend the winter, I winter.
gloss: I spend the winter, I winter

text: παραχειμασία, spending the winter, wintering.
πάρδαλις, a leopard.
παρεδρεύω (adsideo), I have my seat beside, I attend.
gloss: I have my seat beside, I attend

text: παρεισάγω, I introduce from the side.
παρείσακτος, introduced (imported) from the side.
παρεισδύω, I creep in.
παρεισέρχομαι, I come in from the side.
gloss: I come in from the side

text: παρεισφέρω, I bring in (import) from the side, I smuggle.
gloss: I bring in (import) from the side, I smuggle

text: παρεκτός, (a) adv. used as adj., outside, without, left over; (b) prep., apart from.
παρεμβάλλω, I throw (raise) up beside.
παρενοχλέω, I trouble, or perhaps, I trouble further.

παρεπίδημος, a stranger settled in a town or region for a time without making it his permanent residence, a sojourner: so in a spiritual sense of those who are on the earth for a time, whose real home is heaven.
note: entry runs onto page 200; gloss cut short because the first meaning runs to about 100 characters before its first comma

text: πάρεσις (from παρίημι), overlooking, suspension, remission of punishment for.
gloss: overlooking, suspension, remission of punishment for

text: παρηγορία, a consolation.
παρθενία, maidenhood, virginity.
Πάρθος, a Parthian, an inhabitant of the country beyond the Eastern boundary of the Roman Empire between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
παρίημι, (a) I let pass, neglect, omit, Lk. xi 42; (b) I slacken, weary, Heb. xii 12.
Παρμενᾶς (a pet form of Παρμενίδης), Parmenas, one of the original seven ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem.
gloss: Parmenas, one of the original seven ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem

text: πάροδος, way-by, passage.
παροικέω, I sojourn (in), as a resident stranger.
gloss: I sojourn (in), as a resident stranger

text: παροικία, a sojourn in a foreign city or land; so also in the spiritual sense (cf. παρεπίδημος), 1 Pet. i 17.
gloss: a sojourn in a foreign city or land

text: πάροικος (adj. and noun) (= μέτοικος), a stranger, sojourner, in a land not his own, a non-citizen, with limited rights: so, metaphorically, of the Christian resident on the earth, whose real home is in heaven, Eph. ii 19, 1 Pet. ii 11.
gloss: a stranger, sojourner, in a land not his own

text: παροιμία (from παρά and οἶμος, beside the common way), a veiled speech in which particularly high thoughts are concealed, a cryptic saying, an allegory; a proverb (2 Pet. ii 22).
gloss: a cryptic saying, an allegory; a proverb
note: gloss chosen by David, 2026-11-11

text: πάροινος, one given too much to wine, an excessive drinker.
gloss: one given too much to wine, an excessive drinker

text: παροίχομαι, I have passed.
παρομοιάζω, I resemble.
παρόμοιος, like, similar.
παροξύνω, I arouse to anger, I provoke.
gloss: I arouse to anger, I provoke
note: headword printed in active form παροξύνω

text: παροξυσμός, (a) irritation of mind, sharp feeling, indignation; (b) spurring, incitement, Heb. x 24.
gloss: irritation of mind, sharp feeling, indignation

text: παροργίζω, I provoke to anger.
παροργισμός (generally act. provocation), the state of feeling provocation, wrath.
gloss: the state of feeling provocation, wrath

text: παροτρύνω, I urge on.
παροψίς, a bowl, dish.
Πάταρα, Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia.
gloss: Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia

text: πατέω, tr. and intr. I tread; I trample upon.
Πάτμος, Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea, SW. of Ephesus.
gloss: Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea

text: πατριά, a group of persons united by descent from a common father or ancestor, a family, a tribe.
note: gloss taken from the defining words, since the opening description runs over 60 characters with no earlier comma

text: πατριάρχης, a ruler of a family (or tribe), given as an honorary title to David (Ac. ii 29) as ancestor of the race of Jewish kings.
gloss: a ruler of a family (or tribe)

text: πατρικός, belonging to the fathers (ancestors).
πατρίς (patria), native city, native town, native place.
gloss: native city, native town, native place

text: Πατρόβας, Patrobas, a Christian in Rome.
note: headword printed Πατρόβας (acute on ο)

text: πατρολῴας, a parricide, a murderer of his father.
gloss: a parricide, a murderer of his father

text: πατροπαράδοτος, handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited.
gloss: handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited

text: πατρῷος, belonging to ancestors, ancestral.
Πάφος, Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus.
gloss: Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus

text: παχύνω, I thicken: used with καρδία, of obtuseness of mind, it has become obtuse.
note: headword printed in active form παχύνω

text: πέδη, a fetter.
πεδινός, level, low-lying.
πειθαρχέω, I obey one in authority.
πειθός, persuasive.
πεῖρα, an attempt, a trial; πεῖραν λαμβάνειν, to have experience of.
πεισμονή, persuasion, both the act of persuasion and the being persuaded.
πέλαγος, the open sea: in Mt. xviii 6 the use of the two words for sea produces a more impressive effect.
πελεκίζω, I behead with an axe.
πέμπτος, fifth.
πένης, poor.
πενθερά, a mother-in-law.
πενθερός, a father-in-law.
πένθος, mourning, sorrow.
πενιχρός, poor.
πεντάκις, five times.
πεντακόσιοι, five hundred.
note: fifth letter of the headword (α) is damaged on the image; read from context | approved by David, 2026-11-09

text: πεντεκαιδέκατος, fifteenth.
πεντήκοντα, fifty.
πεντηκοστή (originally sc. ἡμέρα; lit. the fiftieth day from 14th Nisan, the date of the Passover Feast), Pentecost, a Feast of the Jews, Whitsuntide.
gloss: Pentecost, a Feast of the Jews, Whitsuntide

text: περαιτέρω (compar. of πέρα, beyond), further, beyond that.
πέρας, (a) a boundary, limit; (b) an end, Heb. vi 16.
Πέργαμον (possibly the other form Πέργαμος, Pergamus, was intended), Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia.
gloss: Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia
note: headword printed Πέργαμον

text: Πέργη, Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia.
gloss: Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia
